turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale, I have a client call at 4:40, so you have twenty minutes. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
"Get this over with." Okay, then answer the question: who entered that zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before they did?
Look, your son cheated. Everyone knows it. I'm not wasting my evening on this.

My son doesn't lie, and "everyone knows" isn't evidence, it's gossip. I'm writing down that you called him a cheater without showing me a single document. Show me something, or I walk upstairs to the principal's office right now.
You lawyers think you can bully anyone.

I haven't raised my voice, Hale, I've asked you for a document. Your own procedure, section 4.2, says a parent is contacted before any mark is entered, and nobody called me. So either you have something in writing about Owen's essay, or that zero comes out today.
Are you going to keep wasting my time?

I'm the one with a client call, Hale, so we'll keep this short. Withdraw the zero and put an apology in writing, or tell me there's nothing more, and I go straight to the principal's office from here. Which is it?
